This is normalization context; the $d^3\mathbf k/(2|\mathbf k|)$ convention and the unitary map $W$ are proved here.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the Hilbert-space supplier. Let $M=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, let $\omega(\mathbf k)=|\mathbf k|$, and equip $M$ with the measure $d
u(\mathbf k)=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega(\mathbf k))$. On $\mathbb C^3$ use the positive Hermitian pairing $\overline u\cdot v=\sum_{j=1}^3\overline{u_j}v_j$ and the complex-bilinear extension of the Euclidean dot product in the transversality condition. Define $\mathcal H_T^
u=\{f\in L^2(M,
u;\mathbb C^3):\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0	ext{ for }
u	ext{-almost every }\mathbf k\}$. Let $\mathcal H_T^0=\{u\in L^2(M,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3):\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0	ext{ for Lebesgue-almost every }\mathbf k\}$ with the second-variable-linear integral pairing. Then $Wf(\mathbf k)=f(\mathbf k)/\sqrt{2\omega(\mathbf k)}$ is a unitary map from $\mathcal H_T^
u$ onto $\mathcal H_T^0$.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Put $M=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, $\omega(\mathbf k)=|\mathbf k|$, and $d
u(\mathbf k)=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega(\mathbf k))$. Define the unit sphere by $S^2=\{\mathbf n\in\mathbb R^3:|\mathbf n|=1\}$ with the subspace topology. For $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$, chart $\{\varepsilon n_j>0\}$ by the other two coordinates in the open unit disk $B_1^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:|x|<1\}$, with inverse $n_j=\varepsilon\sqrt{1-\sum_{i
e j}n_i^2}$; these six charts and their transition maps are smooth. Let $d\Omega$ denote polar surface measure on this sphere. Polar coordinates give $d
u=(r/2)\,dr\,d\Omega$, and every orthogonal map preserves $
u$. The transverse one-photon Hilbert space $\mathcal H_T^
u$ consists of the equivalence classes $f\in L^2(M,
u;\mathbb C^3)$ satisfying $\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0$ for $
u$-almost every $\mathbf k$, with pairing $\langle f,gangle_
u=\int_M\overline{f(\mathbf k)}\cdot g(\mathbf k)\,d
u(\mathbf k)$, linear in $g$. The preceding measure-isometry lemma gives the unitary $Wf(\mathbf k)=f(\mathbf k)/\sqrt{2\omega(\mathbf k)}$ from this space to the transverse space defined with measure $d^3\mathbf k$. The null set $\mathbf k=0$ is omitted throughout.

For $\mathbf n\in S^2$, define $P(\mathbf n)=I-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$. Extend the real cross product complex-linearly by $(\mathbf n	imes v)_i=\sum_{j,\ell=1}^3\epsilon_{ij\ell}n_jv_\ell$, where $\epsilon_{ij\ell}$ is totally antisymmetric and $\epsilon_{123}=1$, and set $h(\mathbf n)=i\,\mathbf n	imes$ and $P_\sigma(\mathbf n)=(P(\mathbf n)+\sigma h(\mathbf n))/2$ for $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$. Each $P_\sigma(\mathbf n)$ is a rank-one orthogonal projector on the complex transverse plane $P(\mathbf n)\mathbb C^3$, and $h$ has eigenvalue $\sigma$ on its range. The fibers $\mathcal L_{\sigma,\mathbf n}=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma(\mathbf n)$ form smooth complex line subbundles of $S^2	imes\mathbb C^3$. Here a smooth line subbundle means a family of one-dimensional complex fibers with smooth local unit sections. The common smooth domain for differential calculations is

$$\mathcal D=\{f\in C_c^\infty(M;\mathbb C^3):\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0	ext{ for every }\mathbf k\in M\}.$$

It is dense in $\mathcal H_T^
u$. For $0<r_0<r_1<\infty$, the mass-shell measure of the radial annulus is $
u(\{r_0\le|\mathbf k|\le r_1\})=\pi(r_1^2-r_0^2)$; in particular $
u$ is sigma-finite.

items.title: Transverse rotations preserve helicity and generate total angular momentum

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, section 6.2.1

references.title: Konstantin Y. Bliokh, Miguel A. Alonso, Elena A. Ostrovskaya, and Andrea Aiello, Angular Momenta and Spin-Orbit Interaction of Nonparaxial Light in Free Space
references.locator: Full 8-page PDF retrieved; section I, equation 1, and section II, equations 6–9, for the total vector angular-momentum expression and helicity Berry connection. The source sets hbar=c=1.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, fix a real parameter $\hbar>0$, and use the transverse Hilbert space, helicity projectors, and dense domain $\mathcal D$ defined above. Let $e_1,e_2,e_3$ be the standard coordinate basis of $\mathbb R^3$. Let $SO(3)=\{R\in M_3(\mathbb R):R^TR=I,\det R=1\}$ with the topology inherited from the Frobenius matrix norm $\|A\|_F=(\sum_{i,j=1}^3|A_{ij}|^2)^{1/2}$. For $R\in SO(3)$ define $U(R)f(\mathbf k)=R f(R^{-1}\mathbf k)$. Then $U$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation on $\mathcal H_T^
u$, and $P_\sigma(\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|)\,U(R)=U(R)\,P_\sigma(\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|)$ for $\sigma=\pm1$. For $\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|\mathbf a|=1$, define $[\mathbf a]_	imes v=\mathbf a	imes v$ and, for $B\in M_3(\mathbb R)$, define the matrix exponential by the absolutely convergent Frobenius-norm series $\exp(B)=\sum_{m=0}^\infty B^m/m!$; put $R_{\mathbf a}(t)=\exp(t[\mathbf a]_	imes)$. Define $(S_{\mathbf a})_{ij}=-i\sum_{\ell=1}^3a_\ell\epsilon_{\ell ij}$, $L_{\mathbf a}=-i\hbar\,(\mathbf a	imes\mathbf k)\cdot
abla_{\mathbf k}$, where $
abla_{\mathbf k}$ differentiates each vector component, and $S_{\mathbf a}^{\mathrm{op}}=\hbar S_{\mathbf a}$. The unique self-adjoint Stone generator $J_{\mathbf a}$ specified by $U(R_{\mathbf a}(t))=\exp(-itJ_{\mathbf a}/\hbar)$ acts on $\mathcal D$ as $J_{\mathbf a}=L_{\mathbf a}+S_{\mathbf a}^{\mathrm{op}}$; here the operator exponential is defined by the Borel functional calculus in Stone's theorem. This total generator preserves transversality, while its orbital and spin terms generally do not separately preserve the transverse space. The stated self-adjoint operators are the Stone generators; the differential expression is their restriction to $\mathcal D$.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $S^2=\{\mathbf n\in\mathbb R^3:|\mathbf n|=1\}$ with the subspace topology and six smooth graph charts: for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $\varepsilon\in\{+1,-1\}$, the chart on $\{\varepsilon n_j>0\}$ uses the other coordinates in $B_1^2=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:|x|<1\}$ and has inverse $n_j=\varepsilon\sqrt{1-\sum_{i\ne j}n_i^2}$. Orient it by the outward unit normal, so an ordered tangent basis $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $u\times v=\lambda\mathbf n$ for some real $\lambda>0$; in spherical coordinates away from the poles its area form is $d\Omega=\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\varphi$. In that chart let $\mathbf n=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\sin\theta\sin\varphi,\cos\theta)$, $\mathbf e_\theta=(\cos\theta\cos\varphi,\cos\theta\sin\varphi,-\sin\theta)$, and $\mathbf e_\varphi=(-\sin\varphi,\cos\varphi,0)$. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ set $e_\sigma=(\mathbf e_\theta+i\sigma\mathbf e_\varphi)/\sqrt2$, a local unit frame of $\mathcal L_{\sigma,\mathbf n}=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma(\mathbf n)$. With Hermitian pairing $\overline u\cdot v$, define the skew-Hermitian connection form $\omega_\sigma=e_\sigma^\dagger de_\sigma$, its curvature $\Omega_\sigma=d\omega_\sigma$, the real Berry connection $A_\sigma=-i e_\sigma^\dagger de_\sigma$, and $F_\sigma=dA_\sigma$. Then
$$A_\sigma=-\sigma\cos\theta\,d\varphi,\qquad F_\sigma=\sigma\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\varphi,\qquad \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^2}F_\sigma=2\sigma.$$
Use the Chern-Weil convention $c_1(\mathcal L_\sigma)[S^2]=\frac{i}{2\pi}\int_{S^2}\Omega_\sigma$ for $\nabla=d+\omega_\sigma$; then $c_1(\mathcal L_\sigma)[S^2]=-2\sigma$. The north and south unit gauges $e_\sigma^N=e^{i\sigma\varphi}e_\sigma$ and $e_\sigma^S=e^{-i\sigma\varphi}e_\sigma$ have transition $e_\sigma^N=e^{2i\sigma\varphi}e_\sigma^S$; the map $e^{i\varphi}\mapsto e^{2i\sigma\varphi}$ has degree $2\sigma$, since its argument changes by $4\pi\sigma$ as $\varphi$ runs from $0$ to $2\pi$. Thus neither helicity line admits a global smooth unit section. This obstruction concerns each line separately and makes no nontriviality claim about the rank-two transverse complex bundle.

items.statement: Let $e_1,e_2,e_3$ be the standard coordinate basis of $\mathbb R^3$. The constant Cartesian circular vectors $e_\sigma^0=(e_1+i\sigma e_2)/\sqrt2$, for $\sigma=\pm1$, form a transverse helicity frame for every nonzero momentum direction; consequently this fixed pair supplies a momentum-independent polarization factor on the transverse one-photon space.
